data.name: Aaniyah
data.gender_notes: Aaniyah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who is full of joy, happiness, and delight. The name Aaniyah carries the meaning “Joy, happiness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Aaniyah usually hope their child will grow to embody joy, happiness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Radiates joy, happiness, and positive energy
data.etymology: Aaniyah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joy, happiness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaniyah total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: عانية
in_arabic.meaning: عانية تعني العودة إلى الله أو الرجوع إلى الله
in_arabic.long_meaning: عانية هي اسم مشتق من الفعل العربي 'عانا' الذي يعني الرجوع أو العودة. في السياق الإسلامي، يمكن أن يعني هذا الاسم الرجوع إلى الله أو العودة إلى طريق الحق. اسم عانية يحمل دلالة روحانية عميقة ويرتبط بالتوجه نحو الله تعالى.

in_urdu.name: عانیہ
in_urdu.meaning: عانیہ کا مطلب ہے اللہ کی طرف لوٹنا یا اللہ کی طرف رجوع کرنا
in_urdu.long_meaning: عانیہ ایک عربی نام ہے جو 'عانا' فعل سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے لوٹنا یا رجوع کرنا۔ اسلامی تناظر میں، یہ نام اللہ کی طرف رجوع یا حق کے راستے پر لوٹنے کی علامت ہو سکتا ہے۔ عانیہ نام ایک گہری روحانی اہمیت رکھتا ہے اور اس کا تعلق اللہ تعالیٰ کی طرف مڑنے سے ہے۔

in_hindi.name: आनीया
in_hindi.meaning: आनीया का अर्थ है अल्लाह की ओर लौटना या अल्लाह की ओर रुख करना
in_hindi.long_meaning: आनीया एक अरबी नाम है जो 'عانا' (आना) क्रिया से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है लौटना या रुख करना। इस्लामी संदर्भ में, यह नाम अल्लाह की ओर लौटने या सही मार्ग पर लौटने का प्रतीक हो सकता है। आनीया नाम एक गहरी आध्यात्मिक महत्व रखता है और इसका संबंध अल्लाह की ओर मुड़ने से है।

in_pashto.name: عانيه
in_pashto.meaning: عانيه د الله تعالی طرف ته راست ورګرځېدنه یا د الله طرف ته مخ اړول
in_pashto.long_meaning: عانيه د عربی نوم څخه اخیستل شوی دی، د 'عانا' کلمې څخه جوړ شوی چې معنی یې راست ورګرځېدنه یا مخ اړول دي. د اسلامي شاليدې په منځ کې، دا نوم کولای شي د الله تعالی طرف ته راست ورګرځېدنه یا د حق لارې پرته بيرته تګ ته اشاره وکړي. عانيه نوم يو روحاني مفهوم لري او د الله تعالی سره تړاو لري.

in_english.name: Aaniyah
in_english.meaning: Aaniyah means return to Allah or turn to Allah
in_english.long_meaning: Aaniyah is derived from the Arabic verb 'عانا' (ana), meaning to return or turn. In an Islamic context, the name Aaniyah may signify a return to Allah or a turn towards the right path. This name carries a profound spiritual connotation, relating to turning or returning to Allah. Etymologically, it connects to the Arabic root 'ع-ن-ى' which conveys the idea of turning or inclining towards something.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aaniyah signifies the essence of positivity, joy, and pride in one's identity. In Islamic culture, it is associated with a sense of happiness and contentment, which is an essential component of living a fulfilling life. The repeated use and popularity of this name among Muslims can be attributed to its uplifting and radiant meaning, adding to the overall beauty and diversity of the Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Aaniyah is a name that evokes a sense of spiritual joy and inner peace. It is a reminder that true happiness and contentment come from within, not from external sources. The name is also a call to live a life filled with gratitude and positivity, focusing on the blessings and joys that Allah (SWT) has bestowed upon us. Internalizing these values and living them out can lead to a spiritually enriching and fulfilling life, embodying the essence of the Islamic faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Joy, happiness" symbolizes The one who is full of joy, happiness, and delight. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Aaniyah serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of joy, happiness.
